earlier_scan.source_named: Only subclassification/wordlist sources on Glottolog (Nurse & Philippson 1980; Maho & Sands 2003); no grammar or phonology of Shubi located.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2018. Change Request 2018-003 (submitted by Bernadette Mitterhofer, SIL-UTB, 2017-09-07; adopted 2019-01-25): split [suj] Shubi / create [xsj] Subi. Dallas: SIL.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Settles identity: Shubi [suj] is JD64, Ngara District, 'very similar to Hangaza [han]' and Rundi; Subi [xsj] is a different language (Biharamulo; close to Nyambo/Haya/Zinza, E.20). Mentions an SIL Tanzania sociolinguistic survey of Nyambo, Hangaza, Shubi, Subi and Sumbwa (May-June 2016) whose findings 'are presented so far in wordlists. The report is still in progress.'

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Shubi language'; LINGUIST List 5.219 (1994) posting by Peter Ladefoged on labiodental stops; Wikipedia (sw) 'Kishubi'.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Ladefoged: 'labiodental stops made by a Shubi speaker whose teeth were sufficiently close together...' (segmental only, no source cited). sw.wikipedia cites Maho & Sands 2002 and Seidel 1898 for Kishubi (the latter misfiled; see above).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page shub1238 (Shubi) and Glottolog reference search (full-text 'Shubi', 10 hits; 'Urushubi', 'Kishubi', 'Waschubi': 0 hits).
sources.note: No descriptive reference (grammar/sketch/phonology) attached to shub1238. Alt names Sinja, Subi, Urushubi. The only phonology-typed record mentioning Shubi is Jouannet 1985 (see below).

sources.citation: Mitterhofer, Bernadette & Louise Nagler (SIL Tanzania Language Assessment Team). 2016-. A sociolinguistic survey of the Nyambo, Hangaza, Shubi, Subi and Sumbwa language communities (Kagera and Geita). SIL Electronic Survey Report (in progress as of ISO CR 2018-003).

sources.note: Contains the sentence '3. Der Wortton ruht gewöhnlich auf der vorletzten Silbe.' (Google Books snippet). Glottolog/Maho assign it to Zinza [zin] JE23 (zinz1238); some bibliographies file it under Shubi. Reading the article's own naming/locality would close the identity question; the statement should be routed to zinz1238. Public-domain full view on Google Books; page fetch was blocked from our machine.
